datasets.title: The Blue Snowball in visible light
datasets.description: ESA/Hubble's picture of the Blue Snowball Nebula, WFPC2: H-alpha 656 nm in green, [N II] 658 nm in red and [O I] 631 nm in magenta, as ESA's page lists them: a bright inner shell inside a fainter outer one, with red knots of slower-ionised gas near the rim. It lies on the walls of those two shells as Guerrero, Jaxon & Chu (2004) fit them to the nebula's spectra: two stretched shells, one inside the other, their long axis tilted 50° from our sight line with its north-east end toward us. Each shell's light is on its near wall and its far wall. No knot's own depth is measured.
datasets.summary: Hubble's picture on the walls of the nebula's two shells, with the shape, tilt and speed its spectra give them.
